flashcard_questions.q: What does “the Word” (Logos) refer to in John’s Gospel?
flashcard_questions.a: Jesus Christ, who existed with God from the very beginning.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Gospel opens “In the beginning was the Word”?
What does Genesis 1 say was hovering over the waters?
What is the literalist Christian view of the creation account?
flashcard_questions.a: God made the world in six twenty-four-hour days, exactly as described.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the liberal Christian view of the creation account?
flashcard_questions.a: It is a metaphor conveying religious truth, compatible with evolution.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the Catholic Church teach about creation and science?
flashcard_questions.a: Faith and science do not conflict; God is behind the Big Bang and evolution.

flashcard_questions.q: What is resurrection in Christian belief?
flashcard_questions.a: The belief that the dead will be raised to new life.

flashcard_questions.q: Which verse does St Paul use to show resurrection is essential to Christianity?
What is particular judgement in Christian belief?
flashcard_questions.a: Judgement of a soul immediately after death, deciding its eternal destiny.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens at the final judgement in Christian belief?
flashcard_questions.a: Jesus returns at the end of time to judge both the living and the dead.

flashcard_questions.q: Which parable describes the final judgement?
flashcard_questions.a: The parable of the sheep and the goats, in Matthew 25:31–46.

flashcard_questions.q: What is purgatory in Catholic belief?
flashcard_questions.a: A state of purification where souls are cleansed of sin before entering heaven.

flashcard_questions.q: What did Jesus say to the criminal crucified beside him?
flashcard_questions.a: Today you will be with me in paradise.

flashcard_questions.q: How does belief in judgement affect the way Christians live?
flashcard_questions.a: They try to live morally, follow Jesus’s teachings and avoid sin.

notes: 14 cards: 4 term→definition (Logos, resurrection, particular judgement, purgatory), 3 tradition→position (literalist, liberal, Catholic on science), 3 belief→source (John 1, Genesis 1, 1 Corinthians 15:17), 2 practice/detail (sheep and goats, Luke 23:43), 2 cause→effect (final judgement, how belief shapes living). Dropped 'judge', 'heaven' and 'hell' as bare glossary terms — they interfere with the judgement cards.
